observations.why: The act of switching to a new, unfamiliar database names novelty and departure from the established as the appealed-to good.
Performance gain and cost reduction appeal to achievement and mastery of craft as the goods that justify the switch.
The arrow notation frames migration as directional progress toward the new, appealing to novelty and change.
Quantified performance gain appeals to mastery and capability of the system as the good.
A fixed timeline frames the migration as a deliverable, appealing to capability to execute on schedule.
